data.title: Gamma benzene hexachloride (lindane, 1%)
data.body:
_More from Khopkar · Scabicides & pediculicides_

**Class:** Organochlorine insecticide

## Mechanism of action
- Blocks GABA-gated chloride channels in mite/louse nervous system → hyperexcitation, death; partly ovicidal

## Indications in dermatology & STI
- Formerly scabies and lice — now second-line only (banned in many countries; withdrawn in India for human use in 2013)

## Dose & formulations
- Historic: thin layer neck down, wash off after 8 h; single application

## Adverse effects
- Neurotoxicity: seizures, death (especially infants, elderly, malnourished, broken skin, repeated use); aplastic anaemia (rare); resistance

## Contraindications
- Infants, children under 50 kg, elderly, pregnancy, breastfeeding, seizure disorders, crusted scabies, broken skin

## Pregnancy & lactation
Contraindicated.

## Viva points
- Neurotoxic — seizures; banned/withdrawn in many countries

_Sources: Khopkar ch.21 (Gamma benzene hexachloride); Wolverton 4e ch.44. Facts summarised in our own words; Wolverton followed where books differ._
